newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu to arrive in U.S. for high-level talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to arrive in U.S. for high-level talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was due in the United States early on Monday for a series of high-level talks.

Netanyahu and President Bill Clinton are expected to discuss the latest Middle East peace moves, including efforts to renew talks between Israel and Syria, as well as the crisis triggered by Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's military offensive against Kurds in northern Iraq.

Netanyahu will meet Secretary of State Warren Christopher at 9 a.m. EDT (1300 GMT) before a lunchtime meeting with Clinton at the White House and a 2:30 p.m. EDT (1830 GMT) meeting with Defence Secretary William Perry.

Netanyahu's visit comes as events in Iraq have overshadowed, at least momentarily, developments in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations. But Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Sunday in London that Israel wanted to move ahead with peace negotiations with the Palestinians.
Netanyahu held a breakthrough meeting with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat last Wednesday, a meeting that Washington pushed hard for and views as a means of giving momentum to the peace process.

The Iraqi crisis was also expected to figure prominently in Netanyahu's talks. Israel was the target of Iraqi Scud missile attacks during the 1991 Gulf War. Israelis flocked to gas mask distribution centres after the U.S. launched missiles against southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday.
